reason: M8 is a VB3-biased PMOS that primarily generates/biases node net027 for the PMOS load device M6; if net027 is biased by another current source (or you accept a different load bias), removing M8 usually doesn’t break the main differential signal path to VOUT1. Caveat: without alternate biasing, M6’s current becomes undefined, shifting VOUT1 DC level and reducing gain.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate (bias/gain shifts unless net027 is provided elsewhere)

reason: M9 similarly biases node net028 for the PMOS load M7; deleting it preserves connectivity but removes the intended current-source biasing on the VOUT2 pull-up branch. Caveat: VOUT2 operating point and output swing may degrade unless net028 is externally biased.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate (main path remains; output bias/swing degrades)

reason: M0 is a VOUT1-controlled NMOS to ground (a local clamp/feedback device) that mainly affects output DC point/linearity; removing it often still leaves a functioning differential stage formed by M1/M3 (bias devices) and M4/M5 (output NMOS) with PMOS loads. Caveat: if M0 is essential for stabilizing or setting the correct VOUT1 bias, deleting it can increase distortion or cause VOUT1 to drift/saturate under some conditions.
